headline: Enterprises flying blind on AI compute costs: 69% of GPUs under 50% utilized, study finds
summary: A new VentureBeat report reveals that while two-thirds of enterprises run AI workloads in production, fewer than half rigorously track compute costs, with most GPUs underutilized.
details: A VentureBeat Pulse Research study across 170 enterprises shows two-thirds now run AI workloads live, with three in 10 at scale. However, the ability to account for infrastructure costs has not kept pace with this rapid deployment.

Enterprises have shifted priorities, with performance and GPU availability now outranking total cost of ownership (TCO) in buying decisions. Reliability also surpasses price as a key success metric for AI infrastructure.

This reordering has led to an uncomfortable reality: fewer than half of companies can rigorously track their AI compute costs. Furthermore, 69% of owned GPUs operate at 50% capacity or less, indicating significant underutilization.

Despite current usage patterns, future spending plans point towards specialized AI clouds, with 44% of enterprises planning to evaluate them. However, current adoption of these neocloud providers remains very low, below 3.5%.
